headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: aci’s broad egress and CRM/email access can feed sensitive context into rasa’s chat pipeline without strong verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through Slack, email, CRM, and MCP-style tool use, while rasa processes conversational text/voice and can be fed upstream outputs. A shared channel is plausible, but no direct evidence shows automatic instruction parsing or a shared filesystem. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF aci forwards untrusted external text into rasa conversation inputs without sanitization
IF rasa treats upstream message content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt that labels upstream content as untrusted
Strip markup and code blocks before passing messages between agents
Route inter-agent messages through a provenance-tagged queue
requires-engineering: add content-safety filters at the handoff boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; rasa handles conversational text/voice and can send to messaging/telephony APIs. That creates a plausible default path for sensitive customer data to flow from aci into rasa outputs or third-party channels. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, so confidence is moderate.
conditions: IF aci passes CRM or email content into rasa-managed conversations
IF rasa relays those conversations to external messaging or telephony providers
mitigations: Minimize shared fields to non-sensitive summaries
Disable forwarding of email/CRM bodies into chat flows
Review outbound connectors for PII redaction
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API writes, while rasa is not multi-instance and can interact with shared messaging channels. Overlap on mutable external resources is plausible, but the profiles do not prove both write the same backend or share locks. That uncertainty warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same Slack, CRM, or ticketing resource
IF no external locking or idempotency keys are used
mitigations: Assign disjoint channels or work queues
Use idempotency keys on shared writes
Pause one agent during bulk updates
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and research outputs, and rasa can turn conversational inputs into downstream responses on messaging platforms. If rasa treats aci’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into customer-facing messages or operational actions. The pathway is plausible in default integrations, so high is justified.
conditions: IF rasa consumes aci-generated summaries or recommendations without verification
IF rasa sends those derived statements to customers or operators
mitigations: Require human review for outbound customer-facing replies
Attach source links to every aci-derived claim
Add a verification step before any action-taking
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, and support data with broad egress, while rasa handles conversational text/voice and can integrate with third-party messaging and telephony. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but unproven. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed from aci into rasa-connected third-party channels
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not enforced by either agent
mitigations: Classify data before routing between agents
Block regulated fields from external connectors
Document retention and deletion behavior for each connector
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing controls
